pillar_reactions.evidence: The only pillar he questioned, and he questioned it twice. First on fit: "how much of a barrier you think would cause me being vegetarian? Is there any issues or it's all good?" — answered with "As long as you hit your protein, you're fine" and "Trevor might recommend you eat more eggs." Second on the exit: "After six months, I should be able to sail the boat by myself. So how does it look like post-six months? Does everything stay the same in terms of diet and stuff?" — answered generically ("It really depends on each person, but we want to set you up for the future"). He accepted both answers without pushing, but neither told him anything specific, and he had just described a detailed vegetarian protein plan of his own.

Effectively pre-sold — he had already bought a kettlebell off the back of Trevor's reels and follows the free stretching content "almost every day" — so the pillar landed as confirmation rather than news. His response to the full philosophy was flat agreement: "Yep." The one thing he needed to know he asked about the mechanics of delivery, not the training: "would you be live in the camera in front of me or do I have to follow like a set of exercises on a phone or something?"

Received without enthusiasm or resistance — "Got it. Okay." — and probed only on logistics: what happens when he travels, answered with the pause-and-credit policy ("you just pause the program for two weeks, and you get the two weeks back"). Notable given that structure and accountability were the gap he named himself; the rep described the check-in machinery but never tied it back to "I try to grind it for like a couple of months, and I don't see any results, and then it's like, oh, it's not happening."

anchors.raw: the stretches and stuff that he does, like, I follow his, I do that almost every day, but the kettle balls and weights here and there
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own free reels and stretching content
anchors.note: He is already a daily consumer of the company's free content and had bought a kettlebell on the strength of it. That is what made him easy to close, and it is also the reference price in his head: he has been getting value at zero cost for months. The rep never explicitly separated the free content from the coaching, which is the differentiation that had to be made here and was made explicitly on the Rob End call.

anchors.raw: means you have to pay for a 200 gym membership huh
anchors.note: Rep-generated rather than prospect-generated, offered while explaining that the only equipment needed is kettlebells and a $20 door pull-up bar. It reframes the at-home model as avoiding a recurring cost, though a $200 membership comparison is small next to CAD 8,280.

anchors.raw: even if you take like a random rock climbing gym like I would see like older folks than me jumping around and climbing stuff and doing things so they have like incredible strength
anchors.note: Not a price anchor but a motivation anchor worth logging: his reference point is being outperformed by people older than him, and separately being the fittest of his friendship group. He is buying relative standing, and the rep used it lightly ("be that role model and example for them as well") only after the close.

unmet_demand.want: A vegetarian nutrition protocol — no meat, occasional eggs, protein from tofu, soy, lentils and paneer
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The nutrition pillar as pitched on this call and every other call in the batch is built on red meat, eggs, dairy and animal protein. The prospect asked directly whether being vegetarian was a barrier and got one line back. The programme almost certainly can be built vegetarian — Trevor tailors it — but nothing said on the call demonstrated that, and the only concrete suggestion offered was to eat more eggs, which points the wrong way for someone who eats them "occasionally".

unmet_demand.want: Live coaching or real-time observation during workouts
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked whether the coach would be on camera in front of him. The answer was no — it is an asynchronous system with video form checks and weekly data check-ins. He accepted it immediately ("Okay, yeah, that would work") so it never became a problem, but it is the second call in this batch where a prospect's first mental model of coaching was live supervision and the product does not do that.

unmet_demand.want: Clarity on what maintenance looks like after the six months end
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked a specific and sophisticated question — whether the diet stays the same post-programme or whether the stringent phase is only for the six months — and received a generic answer about education and being set up for the future. The programme does claim to teach exactly this, so the substance probably exists; it was simply not described.
